newsitem.title: INDIA: India court to consider protecting Rao from arrest.
newsitem.headline: India court to consider protecting Rao from arrest.

text.p: An Indian court was set on Thursday to take up a request by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao for legal protection against arrest in a criminal conspiracy case, court officials said.
On Wednesday Rao's lawyer asked the Delhi High Court for anticipatory bail ahead of a hearing next week in the $100,000 case. If granted, anticipatory bail protects a person against arrest.
On Saturday, a Delhi judge upheld a summons ordering Rao to appear in court on September 30 as a co-accused in the case.
Authorities said that at next Monday's hearing, the court was expected to frame formal charges of criminal conspiracy and cheating against Rao.
The charges carry a maximum penalty of seven years in jail.

Rao resigned on Saturday as head of Congress, India's oldest party, shortly after the judge upheld the summons. He had been under pressure to quit after leading Congress to its worst defeat in general elections that ended in May.
An Indian expatriate businessman, Lakhubhai Pathak, alleges Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.

Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in a failed attempt to secure a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured him at a meeting in a New York hotel that his "work would be done".
Rao has said he is innocent and has denied he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.
The two other accused, Chandraswami and his personal assistant, are currently in judicial custody in Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison located in the Indian capital.
Although a former prime minister and current member of parliament, Rao has no immunity in the case.
Rao's counsel argued in a petition presented to the court on Wednesday that their client was concerned he might be arrested as the two other accused were in prison.
Court sources said if Rao is denied anticipatory bail, he could be arrested on Monday.
The Times of India newspaper said the government was drawing up a contingency plan for medical assistance for Rao if he is sent to jail. Rao has a history of heart trouble.

Rao was replaced on Monday as Congress chief by Sitaram Kesri, 80, a veteran party leader who swiftly reaffirmed his group's crucial support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition.
Legal experts were divided over whether Rao should be granted anticipatory bail.

Newspapers quoted some as saying he should receive the same treatment as the two other accused who are in judicial custody. Others said Rao's alleged role was not the same as theirs, and he deserved different treatment as a former prime minister.
